Subject: Draft for review: Cascade Legal Rights Project response and November 14 clinic update

We’re writing on behalf of Cascade Legal Rights Project to address the concerns raised here and confirm that Saturday’s free tenant rights clinic is still happening.

Receiving a letter from a lawyer shortly after asking for help can be frightening. We understand why that timing would raise questions about how personal information is being handled. People deserve a clear answer without having to share their private circumstances on a neighborhood board.

Our policy prohibits sharing, selling, or otherwise disclosing clinic attendee information to landlords or their attorneys. Clinic sign-in records are retained internally in locked storage.

Magistrate-court eviction filings are public records, and some law firms use those records to send mailings to tenants. Public filings are a likely explanation for the letters described here, but we cannot establish the source of any particular letter from this discussion. We will not discuss anyone’s individual circumstances or confirm whether anyone has attended the clinic.

The next clinic is Saturday, November 14, from 10 a.m. to 1 p.m. The library meeting room will be closed for HVAC repairs, so the clinic has moved to Mt Zion fellowship hall in East Atlanta. The accessible entrance is on the side by the parking lot. The clinic remains free and walk-in; no appointment is needed. Volunteer attorneys and staff can review eviction notices and court papers and explain your options.

You are still welcome, including if you have concerns or questions about the clinic. Please contact clinic@cascaderights.example or call our office at 404-555-0187. For your privacy, please do not post names, addresses, case details, or documents here.

Thank you for giving us the opportunity to respond. We take these concerns seriously and want people to feel comfortable asking questions before seeking help.
